units.title: Actual finite recursive RGO KL error accumulation

sources.label: SPHMC v1 Theorem 6.5 A1 recursive error argument and equation (6.5)
sources.scope: Finite recursive error transfer; numerical stage budgets and concrete sampler guarantees remain separate.

units.boundary: This proves the error-transfer dependency for the actual finite recursive program. Arbitrary supplied Markov Q and L are not identified with the paper smoothed sampler or FORS. No stage accuracy, adequate stopping cap, initialization validity, or expected query-cost bound is asserted. The terminal residual is retained, including on stopped states. All KL values and budgets are extended nonnegative reals. The source A1 Wasserstein accuracy and equation (6.5) still need an actual observation-kernel instantiation.
units.statement: Let E be a finite-dimensional real inner-product space with its Borel measurable structure, and mu any probability measure. States are s=(b,u,k,h) in NNReal times E times Nat times E^Nat. Let a(s)>0 be measurable and theta a fixed nonnegative precision threshold. Define F(s,y) by b_new=b+1/a(s), u_new=(b*u+y/a(s))/(b+1/a(s)), count k+1 and history with y prepended. There exist Markov kernels T,H, constructed before all actual kernels, with T(s) the normalized tilt of mu by -b*norm(x-u)^2/2 and H(s) its Gaussian smoothing with standard deviation sqrt(a(s)). For every Markov observation kernel Q and terminal kernel L there exist Markov P and R_n: P(s)=dirac s if theta<=b and otherwise the pushforward of Q(s) under F(s,.); R_0=L; R_(n+1)(s)=L(s) if stopped and otherwise the bind of Q(s) with y mapped to R_n(F(s,y)). Define e(s)=0 if stopped and KL(Q(s)||H(s)) otherwise, and t(s)=KL(L(s)||T(s)). Both e and t are measurable. For every n and initial s, KL(R_n(s)||T(s)) is at most the sum over j<n of the integral of e under P^j(s), plus the integral of t under P^n(s).
assumptions: E is finite-dimensional over the reals with its Borel measurable structure; zero dimension is permitted. mu is a probability measure.
a is measurable and strictly positive at every state. theta is fixed and nonnegative. Initial precision can be zero or already stopped.
Q and L are measurable Markov kernels on the complete precision-center-count-history state. No probability density or moment assumption is added.
T,H are constructed before arbitrary Q,L. F, P and all R_n have their displayed actual program semantics.
No finite KL, absolute continuity, assumed error measurability, common observation-error budget or terminal-error bound is a premise.

steps.title: Prove measurable fiber KL, including singular fibers
steps.text: Use the jointly measurable kernel Radon-Nikodym derivative and the nonnegative KL integrand z log z+1-z. Fiber KL equals its integral where absolute continuity holds and infinity elsewhere. The absolute-continuity set is measurable; kernel integration and a measurable case split establish fiber KL measurability without a finite-divergence premise.

steps.title: Derive the conditional KL identity in extended reals
steps.text: If the two joint measures with common first marginal are absolutely continuous, identify the joint density with the fiber kernel density and use nonnegative Fubini integration. If they are not, the joint KL is infinite. Were the integral of fiber KL finite, fiber KL would be finite almost everywhere, hence the fiber laws absolutely continuous almost everywhere; this would imply joint absolute continuity, a contradiction.
steps.lean: Local conditional_kl_integral; compProd_withDensity, rnDeriv_withDensity, lintegral_compProd and AbsolutelyContinuous.compProd_right.

steps.title: Obtain the one-step output comparison
steps.text: Apply data processing to the output projection of the two joint laws. Then apply the KL chain rule and the conditional identity. The conditional output error is integrated against the first actual input law, not the ideal law. The calculation involves no subtraction and remains valid when either term is infinite.
steps.lean: Local composed_kl_bound; klDiv_map_le, klDiv_compProd_eq_add and conditional_kl_integral.

steps.title: Construct the actual program and derive ideal consistency
steps.text: Invoke FiniteRGOProgram for the explicit update and threshold. Before choosing Q,L, also instantiate the same construction with Q=H,L=T. Its exact ideal recovery at depth one and its actual recursion show that binding H(s) with T(F(s,y)) equals T(s) on continuing states. This consistency is proved from the parent construction, not included as an assumption.
steps.lean: FiniteRGOProgram.finite_rgo_program; hprog H T, hRIrec 0, hRIideal and hRIzero; main hcons.

steps.title: Establish the recurrence under the actual transition
steps.text: On a continuing state, apply the one-step output comparison to Q(s), H(s) and the output kernels pulled back through F(s,.). Replace the ideal bind with T(s). Push the conditional error integral through F to express it under actual P(s). On a stopped state P(s) is a point mass and every R_n(s)=L(s), so the same inequality holds with e(s)=0 and the terminal error unchanged.
steps.lean: Main stopped and continuing branches; Kernel.comap, actual hrec/hstop/hPf, hcons and lintegral_map.

steps.title: Expand the recurrence into actual visited-law errors
steps.text: Start with f_0=t. Induct on the finite cap, substitute the prior bound under P, and distribute the integral over the finite nonnegative sum. Kernel composition converts the nested j-step integral into the (j+1)-step actual law. Reindexing gives precisely the displayed sum plus the terminal residual. The zero-depth identity uses the point-mass kernel, so no terminal term is lost at n=0.
steps.lean: Local kernel_error_sum; lintegral_mono, lintegral_finsetSum, Kernel.lintegral_comp, pow_succ and Finset.sum_range_succ'.

units.lean_statement: Actual finite recursive RGO KL is bounded by actual state-law observation errors and the terminal residual.
units.lean_proof: Measurable fiber KL, extended-real conditional KL, output projection, derived ideal consistency and finite actual-kernel recurrence expansion.
